ec:2001:q39.question:
The impulse response functions of four linear systems S1, S2, S3, S4 are given respectively by

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - LTI Systems Continuous and Discrete
detailed_solution.markdown:
$h_{1}(t) \neq 0 \text { for } t\lt 0$

Therefores, is non causal

$$\begin{aligned} h_{2}(t)&=u(t)=0 \text { for } t \lt 0 \\ \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} n_{2}(t) d t&=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} u(t) d t=\int_{0}^{\infty} d t=\infty \end{aligned}$$

Therefore $s_{2}$ is unstable and causal

$$\begin{aligned} h_{3}(t)&=\frac{u(t)}{t+1} \\ \text { at } t&=-1 \\ h_{f}(t)&=\infty, h_{3}(t)=0 \text { for } t \lt 0 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore $s_{3}$ is unstable and causal

$h_{4}(t)=e^{-3 t} u(t)$

$s_{4}$ is time invariant, causal and stable

ec:2001:q40.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 40
ec:2001:q40.question: An electrical system and its signal-flow graph representations are shown in figure (a) and (b) respectively. The values of $G_{2}$ and H, respectively are

primary.subtopicLabel: Basics of Control Systems, Block Diagram and SFGs

detailed_solution.concept: Control Systems - Basics of Control Systems, Block Diagram and SFGs
detailed_solution.markdown:
From KVL in both loops In first loop,

$V_{i}(s)=I_{1}(s) Z_{1}(s)+\left[I_{1}(s)-I_{2}(s)\right] Z_{3}(s)$

$V_{i}(s)=I_{1}(s)\left[Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)\right]-I_{2}(s) Z_{3}(s)$

$\frac{V_{i}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)}=I_{1}(s)-\frac{I_{2}(s) \cdot Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)} \; \; ...(i)$

In second loop,

$\left[I_{2}(s)-I_{1}(s)\right] Z_{3}(s)+I_{2}(s) Z_{2}(s)+I_{2}(s) Z_{4}(s)=0$

$I_{2}(s)\left(Z_{2}(s)+Z_{3}(s)+Z_{4}(s)\right)=I_{1}(s) \cdot Z_{3}(s)$

$G_{2}=\frac{I_{2}(s)}{I_{1}(s)}=\frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{2}(s)+Z_{3}(s)+Z_{4}(s)}$

From SFG, $I_{1}(s)=V_{i} G_{1}(s)+I_{2}(s) H(s)$

$I_{1}(s)=V_{i}(s) \frac{1}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)}+I_{2}(s) \frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)}$

$\therefore \quad H(s)=\frac{Z_{3}(s)}{Z_{1}(s)+Z_{3}(s)}$

(comparing above two equations)

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ec:2001:q41.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 41
ec:2001:q41.question:
The open-loop DC gain of a unity negative feedback system with closed-loop
transfer function $\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+7s+13}$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CLTF} &=\frac{G(s)}{1+G(s) H(s)}=\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+7 s+13} \\ \frac{1+G(s) H(s)}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+7 s+13}{s+4} \end{aligned}$$

$H(s)=1$ for unity feedback.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+7 s+13}{s+4}-1 \\ \frac{1}{G(s)} &=\frac{s^{2}+6 s+9}{s+4} \\ \therefore \quad G(s) &=\frac{s+4}{s^{2}+6 s+9} \\ \text { For D.C. } \quad s&=0\\ \therefore \quad G(s) &=\text{open loop gain} \\ &=\frac{4}{9} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ec:2001:q42.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 42
ec:2001:q42.question: The feedback control system in figure is stable

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} T . F . &=\frac{G_{1} G_{2}}{1+G_{1} G_{2} H} \\ &=\frac{\frac{K(s-2)}{(s+2)^{2}}}{1+\frac{K(s-2)(s-2)}{(s+2)^{2}}} \\ &=\frac{K(s-2)}{(s+2)^{2}+K(s-2)^{2}} \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Characteristic equation

$=s^{2}+4+4 s+K s^{2}-4 K s+4 K$

$(1+K) s^{2}+K(4-4 K) s+4 K+4=0$

Routh table is

$$\begin{array}{l|ll} s^{2} & (1+K) & (4 K+4) \\ s^{1} & K(4-4 K) & 0 \\ s^{0} & 4(K+1) & \end{array}$$

For system to be stable,

$$\begin{aligned} 1-K& \gt 0\\ 1& \gt K \text{ and } K \geq 0 \quad \text{ (given in question)} \end{aligned}$$

From third row,

$$\begin{aligned} K& \gt -1 \\ \therefore \quad 0 &\leq K \lt 1 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

A video transmission system transmits 625 picture frames per second. Each
frame consists of a 400 x 400 pixel grid with 64 intensity levels per pixel. The
data rate of the system is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Frames per second =625

Pixels per frame $=400 \times 400$

64 intensity levels per pixel can be represented by 6 bits per pixel.

$\therefore$ Date Rate $=625 \times 400 \times 400 \times 6=600 \mathrm{Mbps}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ec:2001:q44.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 44
ec:2001:q44.question:
The Nyquist sampling interval, for the signal $sinc (700t) + sinc (500t)$
 is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\sin c(700 t)+\sin c(500 t)$

Nyquist sampling rate $=2 f_{m}=700 \mathrm{Hz}$

$\therefore \quad$ Sampling rate $=\frac{1}{700} \mathrm{sec}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ec:2001:q45.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 45
ec:2001:q45.question:
During transmission over a communication channel, bit errors occur
independently with probability p. If a block of n bits is transmitted, the probability
of at most one bit error is equal to

detailed_solution.markdown:
Probability of error =p

Probability of no error $=(1-\rho)$

For error in at most one bit there should either

no error or error in only one bit.

$$\begin{array}{l} ={ }^{n} C_{o}(1-p)^{n} p^{0}+{ }^{n} C_{1}(1-p)^{n-1} p^{1} \\ =(1-p)^{n}+n p(1-p)^{n-1} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ec:2001:q46.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 46
ec:2001:q46.question:
The PSD and the power of a signal g(t) are, respectively, $S_g(\omega ) \; and \; P_g$. The PSD
and the power of the signal g(t) are, respectively

ec:2001:q47.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 47
ec:2001:q47.question:
A material has conductivity of $10^{-2}$
 mho/m and a relative permittivity of 4. The
frequency at which the conduction current in the medium is equal to the
displacement current is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} |\sigma E| &=|j \omega \in E| \\ \sigma &=2 \pi f \epsilon_{0} \epsilon_{r} \\ \Rightarrow \quad f &=\frac{\sigma}{2 \pi \times \epsilon_{0} \epsilon_{r}} \\ &=\frac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 2 \times 10^{-2}}{4} \\ f &=45 \times 10^{6}=45 \mathrm{MHz} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ec:2001:q48.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 48
ec:2001:q48.question:
A uniform plane electromagnetic wave incident normally on a plane surface of a
dielectric material is reflected with a VSWR of 3. What is the percentage of
incident power that is reflected?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} s&=\frac{1+|\Gamma|}{1-|\Gamma|} \\ \Rightarrow 3&=\frac{1+|\Gamma|}{1-|\Gamma|} \\ |\Gamma|&=0.5 \\ \frac{P_{r}}{P_{i}}&=|\Gamma|^{2}=0.25 \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore \quad 25 \%$ of incident power is reflected.

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ec:2001:q49.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 49
ec:2001:q49.question:
A medium wave radio transmitter operating at a wavelength of 492 m has a
tower antenna of height 124m. What is the radiation resistance of the antenna?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{\lambda}{4}=\frac{492}{4}=123 \simeq L$

$\therefore \quad$It is a quarter wave monopole antenna.

So, $\quad R_{a}=36.5 \Omega$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ec:2001:q50.title: GATE EC 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 50
ec:2001:q50.question:
In a uniform linear array, four isotropic radiating elements are spaced $\frac{\lambda }{4}$ apart.
The progressive phase shift between the elements required for forming the main
beam at $60^{\circ}$ off the end-fire is:

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\theta_{\max }=60^{\circ}$ from end fire means 60^{\circ} from array axis.\\ Condition for maximum, $\psi \rightarrow 0$

$$\begin{array}{l} E_{T}=E_{O} \frac{\sin \left(N_{\psi} / 2\right)}{\sin (\psi / 2)} \\ E_{T}=N E_{0}=E_{\max } \\ \psi=\alpha+\beta d \cos 60^{\circ}=0 \\ \alpha+\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} \cdot \frac{\lambda}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{2}=0 \\ \alpha=-\frac{\pi}{4} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.
